text:
Recent work supports separating recommendation plausibility from verifiable evidence. [ANAH (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.442/) annotates individual sentences with reference fragments, hallucination types and corrections. [FIRE (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05225) links user needs to item features and distinguishes recommendation reasoning from generated reviews. Applicable adaptation: attach history item IDs, timestamps and exact title/description spans to each diagnostic claim; these establish observable support, not ownership, satisfied demand or latent preferences.

For this task, use the proposed six labels as operational definitions: immediate choice requires explicit feedback selecting the item now; merely plausible indicates supported relevance without commitment; unsupported prerequisite identifies a documented requirement whose satisfaction is unknown; explicit incompatibility requires affirmative contradictory evidence; duplication requires identifiable repeated items or documented overlapping content; unassessable means available evidence cannot resolve the judgment. Allow duplication and prerequisite flags alongside choice labels. Historical interaction alone cannot establish present ownership or redundant demand. This taxonomy is a task-specific synthesis, not a validated six-class benchmark.

[FaithBench (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-short.38.pdf) provides a useful annotation pattern: labeled spans, explanatory notes, links to source spans and Krippendorff’s alpha. Independently annotate the twenty users’ feedback before adjudication; report raw agreement, nominal alpha, class counts and confusion pairs, with uncertainty clustered by user. [AbstentionBench (2025)](https://github.com/facebookresearch/AbstentionBench) evaluates abstention across multiple insufficiency scenarios; [AgentAbstain (2026)](https://agentabstain.github.io/) uses paired actionable/abstention tasks. Adapt these ideas by reporting coverage, error among assessed cases, unsupported assertions and unnecessary abstention separately. Twenty users support qualitative diagnosis, not strong calibration guarantees; retain macro validation HR@10 for model selection.
